your_private_thoughts_last_10.thought: Turn 2, $1500 cash. EC at $150 is cheap relative to bankroll. Buy rather than auction so nobody gets a discount. Utilities are secondary to color monopolies but 4x/10x rent is fine early income and denies opponents the pair.

EC list is $150. $100 is my ceiling for a single utility this early — acceptable steal, not a war. If p1 or others push past ~$110-120 I drop. Don't burn cash needed for color groups and railroads. p1 already owns States and seems willing to pay; make them pay more or take the cheap utility myself.
Ceiling was $100; $110 is the drop zone. Single utility is weak without Water Works, and cash is better reserved for color groups and railroads. Let p4 sink $110.

No properties, no buildings, no jail cards. A trade now would just signal need and give others leverage. Preserve $1500 for color groups and railroads; single utilities and pinks aren't worth chasing early.

RR at list is a clear buy. $1500 cash, no holdings. Railroads scale 25/50/100/200 and block others from the set. Don't auction a core asset and hand someone a discount. Cash left $1300 still covers color groups.

Only asset is one RR. Mortgaging it is pointless with $1300 cash. No one owns a second railroad or a color pair worth trading for. Don't signal need. End turn and keep cash for color groups and more railroads.

Clear buy. $140 vs $1500 cash. p1 already holds States (pink) plus Indiana (red). Buying blocks them from 2/3 pinks and keeps Virginia as the swing piece. Auction would hand p1 a discount pairing. Cash left ~$1360 still covers railroads and other colors.

$1360 cash, St. Charles + Penn RR. p1 holds the other pink (States) plus Indiana. Virginia still unowned, so a States trade doesn't complete a set and would signal I want the pinks. Don't hand p1 St. Charles. No buildings possible. Don't mortgage. End turn and keep cash for Virginia, more railroads, and color groups.

Clear buy. $220 vs $1360 cash. Reds are high-traffic and high-rent. p1 already owns Indiana (red); auctioning Kentucky risks handing them a second red at a discount. Illinois still unowned, so this is a foothold not a monopoly. Cash left ~$1140 still covers Illinois, railroads, and other colors. Don't signal a red chase in public.

Don't mortgage with this cash. No monopoly possible. End turn and stay quiet about wanting Virginia or Illinois.
